title: The frontend hub carries an Exit details task DR1 does not have — DR1 asks where the consignment goes on to and when it leaves as part of the main reason for import.

finding.frontend: Group 1 of the frontend hub holds a fourth task, 'Exit details', hinted 'Where the consignment travels on to and when it leaves Great Britain' (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/copy/copy.en.js:39-42). It stands for three pages of its own — destination country, port of exit and exit date (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js:35-39) — and it appears with its own status tag whenever the reason for import puts any of those questions in scope. It is absent from the captured hub because the captured notification has no reason for import yet. The 'Main reason for importing' task next to it covers only the reason itself and the internal-market purpose (:34).
finding.prototype: DR1's hub has three tasks in 'About the consignment' and no exit task. Destination country, port of exit and exit date are asked on the reason-for-import page itself, as conditional reveals under the answer that calls for them, and they count towards the 'Main reason for import' task: that task reads Complete only once the reveal's own questions are answered too (app/routes.js:1343-1367). A DR1 user sees one task for the whole of why-and-where-onward, and its status covers all of it.
finding.difference: Fold destination country, port of exit and exit date into the 'Main reason for import' task so the hub shows three tasks in group 1, not four, and so that task's status reflects the follow-up answers as well as the reason. The dependency is the reveal change itself, owned by the origin-and-reason slice: while the three questions live on pages of their own the task row is the only thing holding them, so this cannot land first. Doing it removes the Exit details row and with it the return-route defect that row has today.
finding.falsifiedBy: An 'Exit details' or equivalent fourth task appearing in DR1's 'About the consignment' section for any reason for import.
finding.correction: The finding stands; it was pointing at the wrong picture. SCREENS FIXED: it named fe-hub and dr1-notification-hub, and the task this finding is entirely about does not render on either. fe-hub was captured with no reason for import, so the conditional row is hidden — the string 'Exit details' occurs nowhere in fe-hub.html — and DR1's hub has no such task at all, which is the finding. The one place in the corpus where the row is on a page is fe-hub-exit-details-blocked, captured after this finding was written by driving the journey to temporary admission of horses, and it is now named first. The frontend slot's sentence 'It is absent from the captured hub because the captured notification has no reason for import yet' remains true of fe-hub and is left as it stands; read it as being about that one screen, not about the corpus. The crop the fix produces shows the fourth task exactly as the finding describes it — 'Exit details', hinted 'Where the consignment travels on to and when it leaves Great Britain', sitting under the internal-market row — so the count this finding disputes, four tasks in group 1 against DR1's three, can now be seen rather than taken on trust.

relatedTo.why: this change removes the row the defect lives in
both change which tasks sit in which hub group
